topic: Sharp minimax trial panels for reusable causal validation of deterministic ML updates. Fix finite covariate cells with known positive weights, finite deterministic candidate and future policy libraries with known scores, a budget, bounded outcomes, a neutral action, and nondecreasing Gamma-Lipschitz nonneutral mean responses. Prove sharp intervals with common endpoint SCMs, the exact prospective weighted nearest-matching-score width, a certified budget-optimal rational MILP panel, and simultaneous finite-sample interval coverage. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: exact reductions and bounded enumerations are recorded in <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/exp_mlupdate_reuse_minimax_design.md. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: formalize and implement the rational branch-tree optimality certificate. EARLY KILL TEST: independent three-cell, five-arm exact LP/enumeration comparison.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the budget-optimal reusable-validation panel be equipped with a model-specific rational branch-tree certificate generator and independently implemented verifier whose acceptance proves exact global optimality?

source_refs.claim: The paper derives reusable causal bounds for deterministic ML updates and recommends trialing multiple diverse models, but does not give an exact budget-optimal panel or an independently checkable optimality certificate.
source_refs.author: Jacob M. Chen and Michael Oberst

source_refs.claim: The paper reduces external-validity site selection to k-median and a linear integer program under stated conditions, providing the nearest causal-design optimization analogue without proof-carrying exact certificates.
source_refs.author: José Luis Montiel Olea, Brenda Prallon, Chen Qiu, Jörg Stoye, and Yiwei Sun
source_refs.venue: ACM Conference on Economics and Computation

source_refs.claim: The paper introduces solver-independent certificates for integer-programming results that can be checked using exact rational arithmetic and limited inference rules.
source_refs.author: Kevin K. H. Cheung, Ambros Gleixner, and Daniel E. Steffy

open_problems.why_unsolved: This is a technique-derived transfer from general exact-MIP proof logging to the specialized causal panel objective. Generic VIPR-style certificates rely on LP dual bounds, cutting-plane traces, and a general inference language, whereas the proposed panel certificate prunes a binary tree using the model-specific rational bound B(I,E)=barW(I∪E). The first proof step that changes is therefore establishing that every recorded branch partitions all feasible descendants and that each specialized leaf reason is a valid lower-bound proof. A bounded search found exact rational MIP certification and causal k-median design separately, but no implementation or soundness-and-completeness result for this nearest-matching-score minimax panel certificate.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would provide a formal certificate grammar, a soundness-and-completeness theorem for its branch and leaf rules, an exact-rational generator and independent checker, and a machine-checked certificate matching exhaustive enumeration on every three-cell, at-most-five-arm rational kill-test instance.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation directly frames the repeated-validation burden created by deterministic ML updates and the value of choosing several informative models in one original trial.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: ML models change after deployment -> rerunning an RCT for every update is costly -> one trial should support later causal validation -> the original panel must be selected with an auditable global-optimality guarantee.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its proof-logging separation between an untrusted MIP solver and a small exact-rational checker, proving every branch inference from a restricted certificate grammar.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested result is likewise a proof-carrying discrete optimization of an identification-width criterion, but its specialized monotonicity bound can replace general LP and cutting-plane derivations.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the causal-design-to-facility-location reduction and its integer-program representation, then expose the selected facilities and exact objective evaluations as certificate data.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its k-median support-selection geometry is structurally closest to minimizing weighted nearest matching-score distances over a finite future-policy library.

open_problems.open_problem: What joint choice of trial panel and arm-allocation probabilities minimizes the worst-case finite-sample diameter of simultaneous outer intervals for an entire deterministic future-policy library?

source_refs.claim: The paper explicitly leaves characterization of the minimum worst-case expected width of confidence intervals from experimental data as an open optimality question.
source_refs.author: Vitor Hadad, David A. Hirshberg, Ruohan Zhan, Stefan Wager, and Susan Athey
source_refs.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

source_refs.claim: Joint experimental design and constrained policy choice is generally an intractable finite-sample dynamic program; the paper develops an asymptotically optimal limit-experiment approximation.
source_refs.author: Samuel D. Higbee

source_refs.claim: Finite-sample optimal estimation and honest confidence intervals are derived over Lipschitz outcome classes conditional on the observed support, without optimizing a reusable multi-policy trial panel.
source_refs.author: Timothy B. Armstrong and Michal Kolesár

open_problems.why_unsolved: Population identification width decreases when more informative arms are selected, while finite-sample uncertainty grows when a fixed enrollment budget is divided among more arms and cells. The exact-means nearest-score reduction does not resolve this conflict: its first proof step must be replaced by a finite-sample modulus that combines Lipschitz extrapolation bias, bounded-outcome sampling error, and a maximum over future policies. Existing work treats confidence-width optimality, policy-directed design, and Lipschitz finite-sample inference separately; the scan found no sharp joint panel-and-allocation criterion for reusable partially identified policy values.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would characterize the minimax expected or high-probability maximum outer-interval diameter over panels and allocation vectors, give a finite-dimensional optimization formulation and an attaining design, and prove a matching lower bound under the known randomization.

writing_exemplar.why: It presents experimental-data reuse as a tension between targeted collection and reliable inference for questions not targeted by the design, then poses worst-case interval width as the missing optimality theory.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Targeted experiments concentrate observations -> later policy questions reuse uneven data -> valid intervals may become wide -> jointly choose support and allocation to minimize reusable interval width.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the finite-sample modulus calculation over a Lipschitz conditional-mean class to balance extrapolation bias against estimator variance and construct honest intervals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both targets are governed by Lipschitz distance to experimental support, but the desired modulus also optimizes discrete support and randomized allocation for a maximum over policy values.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the k-median reduction for experimental support while retaining the paper's noisy-effect terms rather than taking the exact-means limit.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest support-selection result combining Lipschitz external validity, sampling noise, and integer design.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its limit-experiment representation and asymptotic design optimization to a partially identified maximum-width loss, then compare it against an exact finite-library formulation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly joins experimental allocation and downstream constrained policy use, although the new loss is reusable interval width rather than Bayes welfare.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the exact joint identified set of the value vector for a finite deterministic future-policy library under bounded monotone Gamma-Lipschitz responses, including sharp extrema for arbitrary policy contrasts?

source_refs.claim: The paper shows that shape restrictions create a nonrectangular response set, so separately optimized pointwise values can correspond to incompatible response curves.
source_refs.author: Samuel D. Higbee

source_refs.claim: The paper gives reusable bounds or estimates for new deterministic ML models from a prior RCT, but does not characterize the complete joint geometry of a finite library's value vector.
source_refs.author: Jacob M. Chen and Michael Oberst

source_refs.claim: The paper treats partial-identification endpoints as optimized values over estimated constraint sets and derives inference by relaxing the estimated feasible set.
source_refs.author: Matthew Tudball, Rachael Hughes, Kate Tilling, Jack Bowden, and Qingyuan Zhao

open_problems.why_unsolved: Common lower and upper endpoint SCMs can establish all marginal intervals and two corners of the value vector without showing that its joint identified set is a Cartesian product. Shape restrictions couple different score queries for the same cell-action response, so arbitrary mixtures of marginal endpoints and pairwise policy differences may be infeasible. The missing step is a support-function or facet characterization of the shared response polytope and a compatibility theorem for endpoint faces; the reusable-validation literature and shape-constrained policy-learning literature do not supply that full vector result.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would give a finite polyhedral or support-function representation of the joint policy-value identified set, sharp formulas or finite programs for every linear policy contrast, and necessary and sufficient conditions for one SCM to attain a specified collection of endpoint faces.

writing_exemplar.why: Its exposition makes nonrectangularity operational by explaining why policy comparisons must evaluate alternatives under the same admissible response curve.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Experiments omit policy-relevant treatments -> shape restrictions bound unobserved responses -> pointwise extrema can use incompatible curves -> reusable policy comparisons require the joint value geometry of one common SCM.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent the shared shape-constrained response class by linear inequalities and optimize both sides of each policy comparison over the same latent response curve.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired joint set is the linear image of the same kind of nonrectangular response polytope; support-function duality extends pairwise regret calculations to the complete value vector.

method_exemplars.technique: Relax an empirically estimated constraint set and derive confidence bounds for optimized values of the resulting stochastic program.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Every support-function face of the joint identified set is an optimized linear functional over estimated shape constraints, making feasible-set relaxation a direct inference route.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one obtain simultaneous finite-sample randomization-only coverage for every sharp policy-value interval in the reusable library when potential outcomes are fixed and the sole randomness is the chosen arm or cluster assignment?

source_refs.claim: Inverting Fisher randomization tests yields finite-sample confidence intervals with guaranteed coverage and permits theoretically justified combination across independent experiments.
source_refs.author: Xiaokang Luo, Tirthankar Dasgupta, Minge Xie, and Regina Y. Liu
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: Randomization-test inversion yields exact simultaneous confidence statements for bounded causal hypotheses and quantiles of finite-population unit-level effects.
source_refs.author: Devin Caughey, Allan Dafoe, Xinran Li, and Luke Miratrix
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: The paper gives asymptotically normal inference for policy evaluation under known adaptive assignments and lists more complex sampling designs as an open direction.
source_refs.author: Vitor Hadad, David A. Hirshberg, Ruohan Zhan, Stefan Wager, and Susan Athey
source_refs.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

open_problems.why_unsolved: Conditional Hoeffding bands under independent sampled outcomes establish a superpopulation statement, not assignment-only validity for fixed finite-population potential outcomes. Exact randomization-inference papers invert sharp or bounded hypotheses about unit-level effects, while reusable validation endpoints arise by optimizing a shared monotone-Lipschitz SCM over unobserved cell-action-score means. The first unresolved step is constructing one randomization acceptance region whose inversion remains computationally finite and whose deterministic image through every lower and upper endpoint program yields joint coverage. The scan found exact randomization inversion and reusable policy inference separately, but not their composition.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would specify an assignment-randomization confidence region under fixed potential outcomes and prove that its lower and upper images through the shape-constrained endpoint programs simultaneously cover every policy-value identified interval with probability at least 1-alpha.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the exact application narrative—one randomized trial reused to validate later deterministic ML models—while leaving room to strengthen the inferential foundation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Repeated RCTs for model updates are costly -> one randomized panel should support later models -> sharp population bounds quantify reuse -> assignment-only finite-sample inference must cover all reused bounds simultaneously.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert bounded-null randomization tests and prove simultaneous coverage by expressing all coordinatewise statements as one confidence set for a latent finite-population effect vector.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested theorem likewise needs a single latent feasible-set event to imply simultaneous coverage of many optimized causal functionals.

method_exemplars.technique: Use confidence-distribution inversion of Fisher randomization tests and exact combination rules that preserve finite-sample coverage.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its assignment-only inversion machinery can generate the joint primitive confidence region before deterministic propagation through the policy endpoint maps.

open_problems.open_problem: How should a reusable validation panel be selected when Gamma is a prespecified sensitivity range rather than a known Lipschitz constant, so that panel optimality and policy conclusions are certified uniformly over Gamma?

source_refs.claim: Breakdown frontiers characterize the boundary in assumption strength at which a causal conclusion fails and support lower uniform confidence bands.
source_refs.author: Matthew A. Masten and Alexandre Poirier

source_refs.claim: The finite-sample optimal estimator and confidence interval depend materially on the imposed Lipschitz smoothness constant.
source_refs.author: Timothy B. Armstrong and Michal Kolesár

source_refs.claim: Reusable validation is based on substantive trust restrictions, but the paper does not derive a panel-design path indexed by a finite Lipschitz sensitivity parameter.
source_refs.author: Jacob M. Chen and Michael Oberst

open_problems.why_unsolved: This technique-derived direction applies breakdown-frontier reasoning to experimental support selection. For a fixed panel, nearest-score costs are clipped piecewise-linear functions of Gamma; after minimizing over integer panels, the identity of the optimal panel can switch at intersections not visible from any single panel's breakpoints. The first proof step that changes is replacing fixed-Gamma optimization by an exact lower-envelope arrangement over all feasible panels and connecting its critical values to policy conclusions. The scan found Lipschitz sensitivity analysis and assumption-breakdown inference, but no uniform panel-optimality correspondence or certificate over Gamma.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would characterize the budget-optimal panel correspondence and minimax width over Gamma, enumerate all exact rational critical values where the optimizer or a prespecified policy conclusion changes, and give a uniform confidence or breakdown frontier for those conclusions.

writing_exemplar.why: It treats assumption strength as a transparent analysis axis and organizes the contribution around the precise point where substantive conclusions change.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Causal conclusions depend on untestable restriction strength -> one calibration conceals fragility -> a frontier records where conclusions change -> trial panels and reusable-validation claims should be certified across the Gamma frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate an assumption-indexed breakdown frontier and construct lower uniform bootstrap confidence bands despite nonsmooth changes in the active constraint.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A Gamma-indexed policy-dominance frontier is the same type of sensitivity object, with panel switches creating additional nonsmoothness.

method_exemplars.technique: Track the finite-sample modulus and optimal honest interval as the Lipschitz class changes, including transitions to nearest-neighbor matching.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its smoothness-indexed optimal-inference path supplies the inferential analogue of the desired Gamma-indexed optimal-design path.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the k-median representation to analyze how changes in distance penalties alter the selected experimental facilities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The panel objective is a robust, action-constrained nearest-facility problem whose optimizer changes as Gamma rescales and clips matching-score distances.

literature_map:
1. Chen and Oberst (2025, UAI; arXiv:2502.09467) establish reusable causal validation bounds for deterministic ML updates and recommend diverse multi-model trials, but do not solve exact budgeted panel selection.
2. Zhang, Skalnes, Chen, and Oberst (2026; arXiv:2607.21806) add counterfactual-correctness and subgroup-performance restrictions and address unknown performance measures, while declining a general sharpness claim.
3. Nercessian et al. (2025; arXiv:2511.08986) develop BRIDGE reuse for concordant medical-AI predictions; its consistency requirement differs from score-dependent response restrictions.
4. Montiel Olea, Prallon, Qiu, Stoye, and Sun (2025; arXiv:2408.09187) reduce external-validity site selection to k-median and integer programming under conditions, the closest experimental-support analogue.
5. Higbee (2025, Quantitative Economics; arXiv:2210.04703) uses shape restrictions and LP/MILP minimax regret for untried treatments, emphasizing nonrectangular common-response uncertainty.
6. Higbee (2026; arXiv:2609.10971) joins experimental design and constrained policy choice but replaces a generally intractable finite-sample program with an asymptotically optimal limit-experiment approximation.
7. Hadad, Hirshberg, Zhan, Wager, and Athey (2021, PNAS) give asymptotically normal policy evaluation after adaptive collection and explicitly leave minimum worst-case CI width and richer designs open.
8. Armstrong and Kolesár (2021, Econometrica) derive finite-sample optimal Lipschitz procedures; their nearest-neighbor boundary supplies the closest inference geometry conditional on support.
9. Kitagawa and Tetenov (2018, Econometrica) and Athey and Wager (2021, Econometrica) establish regret guarantees for policy learning but take experimental support as given.
10. Kasy and Sautmann (2021, Econometrica) design adaptive experiments for final policy choice, emphasizing allocation rather than reusable partial-identification width.
11. Luo, Dasgupta, Xie, and Liu (2021, JRSSB) and Caughey, Dafoe, Li, and Miratrix (2023, JRSSB) provide finite-sample randomization inversion, but not for optimized shape-restricted policy endpoints.
12. Tudball, Hughes, Tilling, Bowden, and Zhao (2023, Biometrika) provide inference for optimized values over estimated constraint sets, a natural route to joint-set support functions.
13. Masten and Poirier (2020, Quantitative Economics) develop breakdown-frontier and uniform-band machinery, suggesting a Gamma-indexed design-sensitivity frontier.
14. Cheung, Gleixner, and Steffy (2017, IPCO) and later exact-MIP work establish solver-independent rational certificates, but no causal-panel-specific branch-tree checker was found.
15. The principal tension is between identification-oriented support coverage and sampling-oriented precision: selecting more arms reduces prospective sharp width but divides a fixed enrollment budget more thinly.
